FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Title: WAL Archiving is Disabled

AdditionalInfo.FindingReason: archive_mode is disabled, so PostgreSQL is not archiving WAL segments for point-in-time recovery.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Recommendation: Enable WAL archiving if point-in-time recovery is required for this PostgreSQL server.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Title: Data Checksums Are Disabled

AdditionalInfo.FindingReason: Data checksums are disabled for this data directory. PostgreSQL cannot detect storage-level page corruption (failing disk, controller, filesystem, or memory faults); such corruption can go unnoticed until it causes a crash or returns incorrect query results.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Recommendation: Enable data checksums (pg_checksums --enable during an offline maintenance window, or via pg_upgrade --data-checksums on PostgreSQL 18+) so PostgreSQL can detect storage-level page corruption.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Title: max_connections Configuration Risk

AdditionalInfo.FindingReason: max_connections is configured above 500, which may create memory pressure and connection-management overhead.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Recommendation: Review max_connections and consider reducing direct database connections by using connection pooling.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Title: statement_timeout is Not Configured

AdditionalInfo.FindingReason: statement_timeout is set to 0, allowing queries to run without a timeout.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Recommendation: Consider configuring statement_timeout to prevent runaway queries from consuming resources indefinitely.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Title: Data Durability Settings Are Disabled

AdditionalInfo.FindingReason: A core durability setting is disabled. Turning off fsync or full_page_writes can cause unrecoverable or silent data corruption after an operating-system crash or power failure.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Recommendation: According to the PostgreSQL documentation, disabling fsync or full_page_writes risks unrecoverable or silent data corruption after a crash. Unless this is a throwaway/bulk-load instance whose data can be fully recreated, set fsync = on and full_page_writes = on and reload (no restart required). For a safer performance tradeoff on non-critical transactions, relax synchronous_commit instead. This changes durability cluster-wide, so confirm intent and validate write performance after the change.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Title: Schemas Granting CREATE Privilege to PUBLIC

AdditionalInfo.FindingReason: One or more schemas grant the CREATE privilege to PUBLIC, allowing any authenticated role to create objects in the schema.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Recommendation: Revoke CREATE from PUBLIC on the listed schema(s) (REVOKE CREATE ON SCHEMA <schema> FROM PUBLIC) and grant it only to the specific roles/applications that need to create objects there. Validate with application owners before revoking.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Title: temp_file_limit is Not Configured

AdditionalInfo.FindingReason: temp_file_limit is set to -1 (unlimited), so a single query or session generating excessive temporary files -- a large sort, hash join, or hash aggregate that spills past work_mem, often from a missing index, a bad plan, or an unbounded report -- can consume all remaining disk space on the temporary file volume. Because that volume is typically shared with WAL and/or table data, filling it can halt writes or crash every database on the instance, not only the session that caused it.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Recommendation: Configure temp_file_limit to a value that bounds per-session temporary file usage without interrupting legitimate large sorts, reports, or batch jobs; review observed temp file usage first, consider role/database-level overrides for known heavy workloads, and test before enforcing in production.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Title: pg_stat_statements is Missing or Not Fully Enabled

AdditionalInfo.Note: pg_stat_statements requires both cluster-level preload configuration and database-level extension creation.
AdditionalInfo.FindingReason: pg_stat_statements extension is not installed in the current database.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Recommendation: Enable pg_stat_statements in a controlled way to support workload-level query analysis. This may require shared_preload_libraries configuration and a PostgreSQL restart depending on the environment. The extension must also be created in each relevant database where query statistics are required.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Title: Deadlocks Detected

AdditionalInfo.FindingReason: One or more databases report deadlocks in pg_stat_database.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Recommendation: Review PostgreSQL logs for deadlock details and investigate transaction ordering, long-held locks, and application concurrency patterns.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Title: PostgreSQL Minor Version Is Behind on Security Patches

AdditionalInfo.FindingReason: This PostgreSQL minor version is missing security fixes released in a later minor release on the same major branch; the most recent PostgreSQL security release fixed multiple actively-exploitable vulnerabilities, some allowing arbitrary code execution or escalation to superuser.
AdditionalInfo.CurrentVersion: PostgreSQL 16.9 on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu-gcc (GCC) 10.5.0, 64-bit

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Recommendation: Apply the latest minor release for the running major branch as soon as possible -- schedule a restart, no compatibility testing is required beyond that.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Title: shared_buffers Appears Very Small

AdditionalInfo.FindingReason: shared_buffers is configured below 128 MB, which appears very small for many production PostgreSQL servers.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Recommendation: Review shared_buffers sizing and tune it according to server RAM, workload characteristics, and production testing.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Title: Synchronous Replication Configuration Review

AdditionalInfo.FindingReason: synchronous_standby_names is empty, so no synchronous standby requirement is configured.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Recommendation: Review synchronous replication configuration against business RPO/RTO requirements and confirm whether synchronous standby behavior is expected.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Title: Autovacuum Cost Delay Is Higher Than Recommended

AdditionalInfo.FindingReason: autovacuum_vacuum_cost_delay is configured above the modern default of 2 ms, which throttles autovacuum I/O throughput and can allow dead tuples and bloat to accumulate on write-active clusters.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Recommendation: According to PostgreSQL operational best practices, review whether the elevated autovacuum_vacuum_cost_delay is intentional. The modern default is 2 ms; higher values throttle autovacuum throughput. Consider lowering it toward the default and/or raising autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit alongside autovacuum worker capacity and I/O headroom. This is a cluster-wide, reloadable change (no restart required) and should be validated against the workload.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Title: random_page_cost May Not Be Tuned

AdditionalInfo.FindingReason: random_page_cost is more than twice seq_page_cost (the traditional spinning-disk assumption). On SSD, flash, or cloud block storage this can bias the planner toward sequential scans instead of index scans.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Recommendation: According to PostgreSQL documentation and community best practices, review random_page_cost against the underlying storage. The default of 4.0 models spinning disks; for SSD, flash, or cloud block storage a value near 1.1 (close to seq_page_cost) is commonly recommended so the planner does not over-penalize index/random access. Confirm the storage type, then adjust and validate query plans. This is a cluster-wide, reloadable change (no restart) affecting all query planning, so test representative queries before and after.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Title: High Temporary File Usage

AdditionalInfo.FindingReason: One or more databases have high temporary file usage.
AdditionalInfo.ThresholdDescription: More than 1 GB temporary file usage since statistics reset.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Recommendation: Review queries that spill to disk. Consider tuning work_mem carefully, improving indexes, rewriting expensive sorts/hash joins, and reviewing temporary file logging.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Title: work_mem Configuration Risk

AdditionalInfo.RiskNote: work_mem is applied per sort/hash operation, not per session. A single query can use work_mem multiple times.
AdditionalInfo.FindingReason: Global work_mem may create memory pressure risk when combined with allowed connection count.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Recommendation: Review global work_mem and max_connections together. Prefer targeted work_mem increases for specific roles, sessions, or workloads instead of a high cluster-wide default.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Title: lock_timeout is Not Configured

AdditionalInfo.FindingReason: lock_timeout is set to 0, allowing sessions to wait indefinitely for locks.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Recommendation: Consider configuring lock_timeout to prevent sessions from waiting indefinitely on lock contention.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Title: log_checkpoints is Disabled

AdditionalInfo.FindingReason: log_checkpoints is disabled, so PostgreSQL is not logging checkpoint activity.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Recommendation: Enable log_checkpoints to improve visibility into checkpoint frequency, checkpoint duration, and storage write pressure.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Title: WAL Compression is Disabled

AdditionalInfo.FindingReason: wal_compression is disabled, so full-page images written to WAL are not compressed.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Recommendation: Review WAL volume and consider enabling wal_compression if full-page-image WAL volume, archive storage, or replication bandwidth is significant.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Title: Pending Restart Settings

AdditionalInfo.FindingReason: One or more PostgreSQL settings have pending_restart = true and require a server restart to take effect.

PendingRestartSettings.Name: unix_socket_permissions
PendingRestartSettings.Description: Sets the access permissions of the Unix-domain socket.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Recommendation: Review pending restart settings and schedule a controlled PostgreSQL restart if the pending configuration should take effect.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Title: log_temp_files is Disabled

AdditionalInfo.FindingReason: log_temp_files is disabled (-1), so temporary file creation is not being logged.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Recommendation: Consider enabling log_temp_files to help identify queries that spill to disk and generate excessive temporary I/O.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Title: Slow Statement Logging is Disabled

AdditionalInfo.FindingReason: log_min_duration_statement is disabled (-1), so slow statements are not being logged.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Recommendation: Consider configuring log_min_duration_statement to capture long-running queries and improve performance troubleshooting capabilities.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Title: log_lock_waits is Disabled

AdditionalInfo.FindingReason: log_lock_waits is disabled, so PostgreSQL is not logging long lock waits.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Recommendation: Enable log_lock_waits to improve visibility into lock contention and long lock waits.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Title: Connection Logging Is Disabled

AdditionalInfo.FindingReason: log_connections is disabled, so successful and attempted connections are not recorded. Connection/disconnection logging is important for security auditing and for correlating sessions in the logs.

FailedChecksThatRequireAttention.Recommendation: According to PostgreSQL logging best practices, enable connection logging for security auditing and session correlation. Set log_connections (on PostgreSQL 18 it accepts a list of aspects such as 'all'; earlier versions are boolean) and consider log_disconnections for session duration. These are reloadable (no restart) but increase log volume, so plan log storage and rotation. If connection auditing is handled by an external proxy or platform layer, confirm that before enabling it at the server.
